title: Connectedness of extensions of affine algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G,Q$ be affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $p:G\to Q$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism, meaning flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and surjective on underlying spaces. Let $L=G\times_{Q,p,e_Q}\operatorname{Spec}k$ be its scheme-theoretic kernel [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $L$ and $Q$ are connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], then $G$ is connected. No smoothness, reducedness, commutativity or separability hypothesis is imposed on any of these group schemes or on $p$.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), printed p.114, exact sequence of algebraic groups, with Proposition 5.45 and Section 5(j) for faithful-flat exactness. In Lemma 16.39, printed p.338, it is applied to a connected kernel which need not be reduced.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-component-quotient] to $G$. Write $c:G\to P_k$ for the resulting surjective homomorphism to the finite constant group scheme. Its topological fibres are exactly the connected components of $G$. This construction applies to the given finite-type affine $G$ without reducedness or smoothness.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), first sentence of the proof, printed p.114; component quotient from Proposition 2.37(b),(d), printed pp.51-52.

proof.text: Let $i:L\to G$ be the kernel inclusion. The inverse images under $ci$ of the summands $\operatorname{Spec}k\subset P_k$ form a finite disjoint open-and-closed covering of $L$. Connectedness [def-weil-connected-scheme] makes exactly one nonempty. It is the identity summand since $ci$ preserves the identity. Thus $ci$ factors through that open subscheme: restrict the morphism and its sheaf map to the inverse image, which is all of $L$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The resulting $k$-morphism $L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is its structural map. Hence $ci=e_{P_k}\circ(L\to\operatorname{Spec}k)$ as scheme morphisms, including on nonreduced test algebras.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), proof: the connected kernel maps to the identity in the component group, printed p.114; explicit open-summand argument.

proof.text: Under the affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum], put $A=k[Q]$, $B=k[G]$ and let $\varphi=p^*:A\to B$. Flatness of $p$ gives flatness of $\varphi$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Surjectivity of $p$ is surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] makes $\varphi$ faithfully flat in the module sense. Apply [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal] to $p$ and $u=c$. Its three groups $G,Q,P_k$ are affine of finite type, its kernel is the given $L$, and step 2 is precisely its required equality on that scheme-theoretic kernel. Obtain a homomorphism $v:Q\to P_k$ with $c=vp$.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), factorization through $Q$, printed p.114; Theorem 5.13, printed p.101. Affine flatness comparison: Stacks Tag 01U5 (morphisms-lemma-flat-characterize); faithful flatness: Tag 00HQ (algebra-lemma-ff-rings).

proof.text: Apply the open-and-closed inverse-image argument of step 2 to $v:Q\to P_k$. Connectedness of $Q$ and preservation of the identity show that $v$ factors through the identity summand as a scheme morphism. Thus $c=vp$ has topological image $\{1\}$. Since $c$ is surjective, $P=\{1\}$. Its sole fibre is all of $G$, and step 1 identifies that fibre with a connected component. Consequently $G$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]; it is nonempty since it has its identity section.

source.place: Proposition 5.59(a), final factorization through the trivial component quotient of the connected $Q$, printed p.114; the finite discrete target argument is written out directly.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 5.59(a), printed p.114, with Proposition 2.37(b),(d), printed pp.51-52, and Theorem 5.13, printed p.101. Connected maps to the finite constant target are checked by their open-and-closed summands.
